tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
docs(doctor): N2 — correct H2's mechanism attribution to libc execvp; DES-077 addendum 2

The H2/rejected-alternative wording claimed "git itself falls back to
running a hook through the shell" on ENOEXEC — imprecise. git spawns
hooks via libc's execvp, not the bare execve syscall Go's os/exec
uses; it is execvp's POSIX-mandated ENOEXEC-retry-through-sh behavior
that gives a shebang-less hook a real execution path, not git's own
run-command.c. The code was already correct (it matches the observable
behavior either way); only the doc comments' explanation of *why*
needed correcting. Fixed in both sandbox.go's doc comments and
DESIGN.md.

Also a one-line nit: RunAll's result slice now pre-sizes to 14 (the
current check count) instead of a stale 6, avoiding a guaranteed
reallocation on every call — not a correctness fix, just avoided waste.

DESIGN.md gets a second DES-077 addendum documenting the S1-S4/N1-N3/
P1-P6 review round in full: findings, fixes, the design ruling to keep
whole-file execution over section-only extraction (and why), and an
updated residual section naming five previously-missing items (P6):
sandbox-vs-reality divergence as the largest residual, Windows
(unchanged), execution-on-dormant-repos (now a decided, pinned
trade-off per P5), exact-argv brittleness (closed, not residual), and
runtime cost (two hooks × up to 10s each on doctor's critical path,
named honestly rather than silently accepted).

`make check` green with race. `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build
./...` exits 0. Detached-env gate: 28 ok packages, 0 FAIL.
EOF
)"
